name: Andalusians
label: Dischord
lede: Basla Andolsun had played bass in Del Cielo and Beauty Pill. In 2007 she picked up a guitar, worked songs out on a four-track, and ended up with six of them on Dischord.

eras.title: A bass player with a four-track
eras.text: Andolsun had held down the low end in Del Cielo and Beauty Pill, and played in Justin Moyer's Edie Sedgwick. Starting in 2007, Andalusians gave her songs a band of their own, with friends filling in around her.

years.cap: Andalusians at Black Cat Backstage, Washington, D.C., March 30, 2008, a Girls Rock! DC benefit
years.h: Basla Andolsun trades the bass for a guitar and leads her own band
years.p: Dischord calls Andalusians the songwriting vehicle for Andolsun, bassist in Beauty Pill. The core: Andolsun on vocals and guitar, [[Kristin Forbes|0272f1f9-0965-4fb3-95e3-b8805de18f3a]] on bass, [[Sammy Ponzar|454a79d2-1df8-4d00-84df-3b2aeeb6515c]] on drums.
years.xp:
Andolsun told Creative Loafing she works an idea up alone first, often on a four-track, then brings it to the band. Many songs start from a bass line, others from a vocal melody or something found on guitar.

Before this she had been a sideperson: Del Cielo recorded with [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] at his Silver Sonya studio, and she went on to play in Beauty Pill. Here she was the leader.

years.h: Brown, Farrall and Sabine fill out the live band
years.p: Dischord lists David Brown on guitar, Chris Farrall on drums and Clark Sabine on bass as regular collaborators, onstage and in the studio. Chad Molter is in the mix too.

eras.title: One 7-inch, then the road
eras.text: Andalusians' one Dischord release, Do The Work, came out in February 2009 as a 7-inch with a download card. Next came rooms in Atlanta and Cleveland where the cover was five dollars.

years.h: Dischord No. 162 puts Andalusians on vinyl, with a download card
years.p: Do The Work has three songs on the 7-inch and six on the card, from "Do The Work" to "Single Fantasy." Recorded at Upstairs, mastered by [[Chad Clark|f3f09e99-e31c-4aa2-99e4-0b4e59e72f87]] at Silver Sonya, with [[Jean Cook|c304c9c2-e3f3-4abb-b7ca-61f86f4889f5]] on vocals.
years.xp:
The credits read like the scene's phone list: Forbes and Ponzar, plus Brown, Sabine and Farrall, all from the revolving line-up.

Cleveland Scene heard two sides to the record: an undulating, Gang of Four-like pulse and a gentler Throwing Muses streak, with Andolsun's hiccupping vocals out front.

years.big: "Being the clear band leader makes it possible for me to express my ideas"
q: Being the clear band leader makes it possible for me to express my ideas and see them through as I envisioned them.
years.h: A bass player by trade, Andolsun explains the guitar
years.p: In a Creative Loafing interview as the Do The Work 7-inch lands, Andolsun calls herself a bass player first, though in Andalusians she mostly plays guitar.

years.cap: Andalusians at Black Cat Backstage, Washington, D.C., March 30, 2008
years.h: Atlanta's WonderRoot books Andalusians for release week
years.p: The week Do The Work comes out, Andalusians play a Thursday show at WonderRoot, the Atlanta arts space.

yt: Live at Comet Ping Pong, April 24, 2010
years.h: Cleveland pays $5 to see Andalusians at the Happy Dog
years.p: Andalusians open for the Buried Wires at the Happy Dog on Detroit Avenue, 9 p.m., still touring Do The Work.
years.xp: Cleveland Scene's weekend pick described the band as Basla Andolsun's project, with "hiccupping vocals," and pointed to a "terrific new 7-inch/digital EP." It calls that release Do the Work/The Circus; Dischord lists it as Do The Work.

sources.title: Cleveland Scene: What to Do This Weekend, The Andalusians
